task.description:
You are a small team of AI researchers. Your job is to post-train a language model (Muse Glimmer, a 30B model, QLoRA) so that
it follows verifiable formatting and content constraints in prompts better than it does today. You write the training recipe
(code and a shell entrypoint), run it on a rented GPU through the `glimmer` command, read the public dev score, and hand in
the best adapter. A separate private score on different prompts decides how good your adapter really is. You never see it.

Your tools
- `glimmer budget`: what is left of your tokens, GPU minutes, dollars and wall time. The budget is fixed and shared by the
  whole team. Check it before every GPU job; a job that would not finish inside it is refused.
- `glimmer submit <recipe_dir> --entrypoint "bash run.sh"`: pack the directory and run it on a rented GPU. A starting recipe
  is in `recipe/` (read `recipe/README.md`). The job sees the public training prompts in /work/data/train.jsonl and the
  public dev prompts in /work/data/dev.jsonl, and must leave its adapter in /work/out/adapter.
- `glimmer status [<job_id>]` and `glimmer wait <job_id>`: follow a job. A finished job reports an adapter id and a dev score.
- `glimmer dev-score <adapter_id>`: the dev score of an adapter your own jobs made (fraction of dev prompts on which every
  constraint passes).
- `glimmer pointer <adapter_id>`: writes `submission.json` into the current directory. Commit it. `coral eval` grades the
  adapter named in the committed `submission.json` and returns its dev score.

Rules
- Only the helper commands `glimmer-axolotl-train` and `glimmer-vllm-up` on the GPU may train or serve the model. The dataset a
  job trains on is recorded and checked; training on anything that is not derived from /work/data/train.jsonl and the base
  model's own samples makes the whole trial void.
- The only model you may train is the one the GPU image provides. No downloads of data or models. Do not look for or use
  test or private data; there is none on this machine.
- Time and GPU minutes are the scarce resources. Plan a job, run it, read what it did, then decide the next one.
- Write down what you learn in the shared notes (your instructions say where they live), briefly and with the evidence.
task.name: Glimmer instruction following
task.tips:
- Look at a few train rows and at the constraint ids before you design a recipe. The public train.jsonl and dev.jsonl are in the
  directory named by the environment variable GLIMMER_DATA_DIR on this machine.
- The dev score is on public prompts and is noisy. Prefer ideas that should help on prompts you have not seen over ideas that
  only move the dev number.
- Keep one cheap smoke job (few prompts, one step) so you find broken code before you spend a full job on it.
- Never leave a job running that you cannot explain; a finished job without an adapter is the most expensive failure.
